title: Answers the Attorney General's registry objected to in writing
question: In which years did the State registry itself write to a City-funded charity that an answer on its yearly report was wrong or that a required audit was missing?
finding: 86 incomplete-report letters to these organizations were read. 13 objections go to the substance of a report rather than a fee, a signature or a missing page: 6 years at 2 organizations (Freedom West Homes Corporation, La Cocina) in which the registry wrote that an independent audit was required and the report said none was done; 1 in which a "No" on transactions with officers or directors was contradicted by Schedule L; and 5 in which a "No" on government funding was contradicted by the return.
how: Every letter the registry labels an incomplete-report notice was read as text and searched for four fixed sentences the registry uses. Letters about the same report year are counted together; the first and last letter dates are shown. For audit objections the registry's document list is checked for an audited statement received after the first letter. City payments are those of the City fiscal years that overlap the report year.
limits: These are requests to correct or explain, not findings of wrongdoing, and most were answered. The registry's letter states only that an audit "appears" to have been required; an organization can answer that it was exempt. An audit received later may cover different years from the ones asked about: the statement itself has to be read. Letters before 2017 and letters the registry did not publish are not covered.
